title: senders.*.dkim.type takes any value, and a lower-case cname reads as a HALF PAIR over a zone that holds it
body:
## Problem

`senders.*.dkim.type` takes any value. Its two rows in `_INFRA_PROFILE_KEYS` (`lib/infra:441`, `:444`) carry no allowed-words column, so a profile with `cname`, `Cname`, `txt` or `bogus` is accepted. `infra check` then passes the value as written (`lib/infra.check:281`, `:291`) to `infra_dns_rrset`, whose `TXT)` match is case-sensitive, and `_idns_rows` keeps only answers whose type equals it exactly; dig prints types in upper case, so `cname` keeps nothing and the check reports a HALF PAIR over a zone that carries the record. A false red, and a value no check can ever hold. Parked at the 0.1.8 cut (from 0143); fixed forward in the bundle on hv's word, 2026-10-03.

## Measured at 2ce9411 (0152 v1 on 953d040; cc's evidence pass)

`infra show --profile` exits 0 for `cname`, `Cname`, `txt` and `bogus`; the control, `dmarc.policy: Reject`, is refused. Through a fake dig that reads the type case-insensitively and answers in upper case, as dig does: `CNAME` holds (2 held, 0 drift, rc 0); `cname` and `Cname` report HALF PAIR, rc 1; `TXT` holds and `txt` reports HALF PAIR. The suite's own fake refuses `cname` outright (exit 64), so through it the same profile reads NOT MEASURED, which is why the suite cannot see this.

## Fix

Both rows allow only `CNAME` and `TXT`, so a bad value is refused when the profile is read, naming the key and the two words, before any query. The reference profile and the infra page state the two words.

## Done when

1. A profile with `dkim.type: cname`, and one with `bogus`, are each refused by name when read; red at 2ce9411.
2. Such a profile makes no DNS query.
3. `CNAME` and `TXT` still hold over a zone that carries them.

## Resolution

Fixed at aa1c1776. `senders.*.dkim.type` takes only `CNAME` or `TXT`: both rows in `_INFRA_PROFILE_KEYS` now carry the two words, so the table-driven validator refuses any other value when the profile is read, naming the key and the words, before any query. The infra page and the reference profile's comment state them. An absent type still defaults to CNAME; an explicit empty one is now refused as a value it does not take, which no arm tests.

Against the done-when list:

1. A profile with `dkim.type: cname` on a single-record sender, and one with `bogus` on a labelled sender, are each refused by name when read: infra-check.bats's (0161) arm, red on the code beneath this change, where nothing refused and the run went to dig.
2. Such a profile makes no DNS query: the same arm holds the fake dig's query log empty.
3. `CNAME`, `TXT`, and `TXT` in the labelled form still hold over a zone that carries them, the run passing: the positive-control arm.

Evidence. 3 mutants, all killed. The arms run green under GNU coreutils, findutils and sed as well as the BSD tools. The full suite on the landing tree: vc's full suite, on main af758c10 (code at 415ce738) with 0163 v3.1 and 0167 git-am'd and cc's 0155, 0160, 0161 and 0162 applied above them, in a fresh clone: 2190 of 2190 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261006-0607), 06:07:26Z to 06:55:27Z; 5 skipped, the expected five: two arms that need a runner with no controlling terminal, two require_command arms whose expected outcome is a skip, and a case-folding disk.
